question: Why does Paul not mean keeping away from all the fornicators of this world?
choices: Then they must needs go out of the world
explanation: Then must ye needs go out of the world.

question: What are they told not to do with such a brother?
explanation: If any man that is called a brother be a fornicator, with such an one no not to eat.

question: Why does Paul say to deliver the man to Satan?
choices: That he may be put to death
That the church may be warned
That he may leave the city
That the spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord Jesus
explanation: To deliver such an one unto Satan for the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord Jesus.

question: Which of these does Paul name among those he says not to keep company with?
explanation: If any man that is called a brother be a fornicator, or covetous, or an idolater, or a railer, or a drunkard, or an extortioner.

question: Whom does Paul say he has nothing to do with judging?
explanation: For what have I to do to judge them also that are without?

question: Who judges them that are without?
explanation: But them that are without God judgeth.

question: How does Paul say he is with them, though absent in body?
explanation: I verily, as absent in body, but present in spirit, have judged already.

question: In whose name should the church be gathered to act?
explanation: In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, when ye are gathered together, and my spirit.

question: Besides old leaven, what leaven must the feast be kept without?
explanation: Not with old leaven, neither with the leaven of malice and wickedness.

question: Whom does Paul say the church ought to judge?
explanation: Do not ye judge them that are within?

question: Whom shall the saints judge besides the world?
explanation: Know ye not that we shall judge angels?

question: What does Paul say they should rather do than go to law?
explanation: Why do ye not rather take wrong? why do ye not rather suffer yourselves to be defrauded?

question: Who shall not inherit the kingdom of God?
explanation: Know ye not that the unrighteous shall not inherit the kingdom of God?

question: What had happened to the Corinthians who were once among the unrighteous?
choices: They were washed, sanctified and justified
They were fasted and prayed over
explanation: Such were some of you: but ye are washed, but ye are sanctified, but ye are justified in the name of the Lord Jesus.

question: What will God do for believers, as he raised up the Lord?
choices: Raise us up by his own power
explanation: God hath both raised up the Lord, and will also raise up us by his own power.

question: Before whom do brother and brother go to law?
explanation: But brother goeth to law with brother, and that before the unbelievers.

question: Whom does Paul say to set to judge matters of this life?
choices: Them who are least esteemed in the church
explanation: Set them to judge who are least esteemed in the church.

question: What does Paul ask is not found among them, to judge between brethren?
explanation: Is it so, that there is not a wise man among you? no, not one that shall be able to judge between his brethren?

question: What does Paul say they do to their brethren?
explanation: Nay, ye do wrong, and defraud, and that your brethren.

question: What does Paul say of all things that are lawful for him?
explanation: All things are lawful unto me, but all things are not expedient.

question: What does Paul say the bodies of believers are?
explanation: Know ye not that your bodies are the members of Christ?

question: What does Paul say of him who is joined to a harlot?
choices: He is one body with her
He is cut off from the law
He is under the law of Moses
explanation: He which is joined to an harlot is one body: for two, saith he, shall be one flesh.

question: What is he that is joined to the Lord?
explanation: But he that is joined unto the Lord is one spirit.

question: Against what does the fornicator sin?
explanation: He that committeth fornication sinneth against his own body.

question: What does Paul say believers are not?
explanation: Ye are not your own.

question: What will God do to the belly and meats?
explanation: Meats for the belly, and the belly for meats: but God shall destroy both it and them.

question: For whom is the body, according to Paul, rather than for fornication?
explanation: Now the body is not for fornication, but for the Lord; and the Lord for the body.

question: Which of these does Paul say shall not inherit the kingdom of God?
explanation: Nor thieves, nor covetous, nor drunkards, nor revilers, nor extortioners, shall inherit the kingdom of God.

question: If the saints shall judge the world, what does Paul say they are not unworthy to judge?
explanation: If the world shall be judged by you, are ye unworthy to judge the smallest matters?

question: What warning does Paul give before listing the unrighteous?
explanation: Be not deceived: neither fornicators, nor idolaters, nor adulterers.

question: How does Paul answer the thought of making the members of Christ the members of a harlot?
explanation: Shall I then take the members of Christ, and make them the members of an harlot? God forbid.

question: What does Paul quote saying the two shall be?
explanation: For two, saith he, shall be one flesh.

question: From whom do believers have the Holy Ghost?
explanation: Your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God.

question: In what two things does Paul say to glorify God?
explanation: Therefore glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God’s.

question: Instead of before the saints, before whom does Paul ask if any dare go to law?
explanation: Dare any of you, having a matter against another, go to law before the unjust, and not before the saints?

question: When is a wife free to be married to whom she will?
explanation: The wife is bound by the law as long as her husband liveth; but if her husband be dead, she is at liberty to be married to whom she will.

question: What should the husband render unto the wife?
explanation: Let the husband render unto the wife due benevolence: and likewise also the wife unto the husband.

question: What does Paul say every man has of God?
explanation: Every man hath his proper gift of God, one after this manner, and another after that.

question: What does Paul say is better than to burn?
explanation: But if they cannot contain, let them marry: for it is better to marry than to burn.

question: What does the Lord command the wife not to do?
explanation: Unto the married I command, yet not I, but the Lord, Let not the wife depart from her husband.

question: If the unbelieving partner departs, what does Paul say?
explanation: But if the unbelieving depart, let him depart.

question: What matters, since circumcision is nothing and uncircumcision is nothing?
choices: The keeping of the commandments of God
explanation: Circumcision is nothing, and uncircumcision is nothing, but the keeping of the commandments of God.

question: What does Paul tell them not to be, since they are bought with a price?
explanation: Ye are bought with a price; be not ye the servants of men.

question: What does Paul say to one called being a servant?
explanation: Art thou called being a servant? care not for it: but if thou mayest be made free, use it rather.

question: What does Paul say about the time?
explanation: But this I say, brethren, the time is short.

question: What does Paul say he has not about virgins?
explanation: Now concerning virgins I have no commandment of the Lord: yet I give my judgment.

question: Why might a couple part for a time, by consent?
choices: To give themselves to fasting and prayer
explanation: Defraud ye not one the other, except it be with consent for a time, that ye may give yourselves to fasting and prayer.

question: Why should they come together again after fasting and prayer?
explanation: Come together again, that Satan tempt you not for your incontinency.

question: How does Paul say he speaks about their coming together again?
explanation: But I speak this by permission, and not of commandment.

question: If a wife departs, what must she do?
choices: Remain unmarried or be reconciled to her husband
explanation: But and if she depart, let her remain unmarried, or be reconciled to her husband.

question: What should a brother do whose unbelieving wife is pleased to dwell with him?
explanation: If any brother hath a wife that believeth not, and she be pleased to dwell with him, let him not put her away.

question: What does Paul say of the children when one parent believes?
explanation: Else were your children unclean; but now are they holy.

question: What does Paul ask the wife?
choices: Whether she shall save her husband
explanation: For what knowest thou, O wife, whether thou shalt save thy husband?

question: Where does Paul say he ordains this rule?
explanation: As the Lord hath called every one, so let him walk. And so ordain I in all churches.

question: What does Paul tell a circumcised man who is called?
explanation: Is any man called being circumcised? let him not become uncircumcised.

question: What is the servant who is called in the Lord?
explanation: He that is called in the Lord, being a servant, is the Lord’s freeman.

question: What does Paul tell a man who is bound unto a wife?
explanation: Art thou bound unto a wife? seek not to be loosed.

question: What does Paul say about one who marries?
explanation: But and if thou marry, thou hast not sinned; and if a virgin marry, she hath not sinned.

question: What does Paul wish for the Corinthians?
explanation: But I would have you without carefulness.

question: What does Paul say he does not want to cast upon them?
explanation: Not that I may cast a snare upon you, but for that which is comely.

question: What does Paul say makes a widow happier?
explanation: But she is happier if she so abide, after my judgment.

question: What does Paul say is good for a man, in answer to what they wrote?
explanation: Now concerning the things whereof ye wrote unto me: It is good for a man not to touch a woman.

question: What is the woman with an unbelieving husband told, if he is pleased to dwell with her?
explanation: If he be pleased to dwell with her, let her not leave him.

question: What is a brother or sister not under, when the unbeliever departs?
explanation: A brother or a sister is not under bondage in such cases: but God hath called us to peace.

question: For what does Paul think it good for a man to remain as he is?
explanation: I suppose therefore that this is good for the present distress.

question: How should those who have wives be, says Paul?
explanation: The time is short: it remaineth, that both they that have wives be as though they had none.

question: How should they that weep be, says Paul?
explanation: And they that weep, as though they wept not.

question: What does Paul say passeth away?
explanation: For the fashion of this world passeth away.

question: How does the unmarried woman seek to be holy?
choices: Both in body and in spirit
explanation: The unmarried woman careth for the things of the Lord, that she may be holy both in body and in spirit.

question: Why does Paul speak, so they may attend upon the Lord?
explanation: That ye may attend upon the Lord without distraction.

question: If his virgin passes the flower of her age, what may a man do?
choices: Let them marry; he sinneth not
explanation: If she pass the flower of her age, and need so require, let him do what he will, he sinneth not: let them marry.

question: What does Paul say of the man who stands stedfast in his heart and keeps his virgin?
explanation: He that standeth stedfast in his heart, having no necessity, but hath power over his own will, and hath so decreed in his heart that he will keep his virgin, doeth well.

question: What does Paul say of him that giveth her not in marriage?
explanation: He that giveth her in marriage doeth well; but he that giveth her not in marriage doeth better.

question: In whom only is a widow free to marry?
explanation: She is at liberty to be married to whom she will; only in the Lord.

question: What does Paul think he has?
explanation: I think also that I have the Spirit of God.

question: Of what has Paul obtained mercy, as he gives his judgment?
choices: Of the Lord, to be faithful
explanation: I give my judgment, as one that hath obtained mercy of the Lord to be faithful.

question: What does Paul say an idol is?
explanation: We know that an idol is nothing in the world, and that there is none other God but one.

question: To whom must their liberty not become a stumblingblock?
explanation: Take heed lest by any means this liberty of yours become a stumblingblock to them that are weak.

question: Through your knowledge, who shall perish, for whom Christ died?
explanation: Through thy knowledge shall the weak brother perish, for whom Christ died?

question: What does Paul say of the man who thinks he knows any thing?
choices: He knows nothing yet as he ought to know
explanation: If any man think that he knoweth any thing, he knoweth nothing yet as he ought to know.

question: What is true of the man who loves God?
explanation: But if any man love God, the same is known of him.

question: What does Paul say there be that are called gods, in heaven or in earth?
explanation: Though there be that are called gods, whether in heaven or in earth, as there be gods many, and lords many.

question: What does Paul say some still have when they eat meat offered to idols?
explanation: Some with conscience of the idol unto this hour eat it as a thing offered unto an idol.

question: What does Paul say about whether eating makes us better?
choices: We are better if we eat
We are not the better if we eat, nor the worse if we eat not
We are worse if we eat
We are judged by what we eat
explanation: Neither, if we eat, are we the better; neither, if we eat not, are we the worse.

question: Where does Paul picture the man with knowledge sitting at meat?
choices: In a house of the weak
explanation: If any man see thee which hast knowledge sit at meat in the idol’s temple.

question: Whom do they sin against when they wound the weak conscience?
explanation: When ye sin so against the brethren, and wound their weak conscience, ye sin against Christ.

question: What does Paul say is not in every man?
explanation: Howbeit there is not in every man that knowledge.

question: What happens to the weak conscience, when the weak eat as a thing offered to an idol?
explanation: Their conscience being weak is defiled.

question: What would the weak man’s conscience be emboldened to do?
choices: Eat the things offered to idols
explanation: Shall not the conscience of him which is weak be emboldened to eat those things which are offered to idols?

question: By whom are all things, and we by him?
explanation: And one Lord Jesus Christ, by whom are all things, and we by him.

question: Of whom are all things, and we in him?
explanation: But to us there is but one God, the Father, of whom are all things, and we in him.

question: What does Paul say we all have, concerning things offered to idols?
explanation: Now as touching things offered unto idols, we know that we all have knowledge.

question: What does Paul say there is none other of, besides an idol being nothing?
explanation: An idol is nothing in the world, and that there is none other God but one.
